newsitem.title: CANADA: Mining industry urges Canada to streamline rules.
newsitem.headline: Mining industry urges Canada to streamline rules.

text.p: The Canadian government needs to streamline mining regulations to make Canada a more attractive place to invest, a mining lobby group said Wednesday.
"We are simply seeking more certainty and a reduction in the amount of red tape currently scaring investors away," said spokeswoman Eileen Wykes of industry lobby group Keep Mining in Canada.
"Delays and uncertainty affect the Canadian mining industry's international competitiveness and threaten mining's position as a cornerstone of the modern economy," she said in a statement.
The group, which has a campaign once a year, has been urging the federal government to harmonize provincial and federal regulations, especially in the area of the environment.

Companies have complained that approvals for mining take far longer in Canada than in many other countries because of overlapping environmental approval processes and outstanding aboriginal land claims.
But Ottawa says its new mining policy announced earlier this week goes a long way toward addressing the mining industry's concerns.

"The policy sets out as one of its key objectives to reduce and eliminate duplication" of provincial and federal regulations, Pierre Gratton, press secretary to the Minister of Natural Resources, said in an interview from Ottawa.
"What we're doing is what the mining industry wants us to do."
Meanwhile, the Mining Association of Canada released a study Wednesday on voluntary emissions reduction.
Mining companies accounting for 92 percent of Canada's base metal production have reduced emissions of 12 major substances by 68 percent since 1988, the study said.
The companies have already met targets set for the year 2000, the association said.
